{"relevant": true, "severity": "critical", "message": "internal/auth/reset.go: token = md5(email + timestamp) is predictable. An attacker who knows a victim's email can guess the request time (seconds or ms) and brute-force the token to take over the account. Fix: generate 32 bytes from crypto/rand, base64url-encode, and store only its SHA-256 hash with user ID and a short expiry (~15-30 min). Make it single-use and invalidate it on use or when the password changes. Also: return the same response whether or not the email exists, compare hashes with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, rate-limit POST /reset per IP and per account, and invalidate existing sessions after a reset."}
